title: Scoped proof: R420 quad4 all-length cleanup minimum is 9
body:
PR1266 establishes reverse-positive cleanup norm 9 among shortest 11-ADD words for Chris Barber's fixed R420 quad-4 transfer, while leaving longer words open. This contribution proves that **every finite positive-ADD factorization of that same ordered six-register integer target has norm at least 9**. The existing 11-ADD witness attains the floor, so the all-length minimum is exactly 9. No new circuit witness or kappa is attributed here.

The proof combines three necessary invariants: the reverse-positive matrix Q majorizes the entrywise absolute signed inverse, Q has positive diagonal, and Q is congruent to the signed inverse modulo two. In inverse row `[-1, 0, 1, -3, 1, -1]`, the zero diagonal forces an even positive Q diagonal of at least two, raising the former absolute-inverse row floor from 7 to 9. The argument covers arbitrary word length without enlarging the predecessor search.

Reproduce the registered package (Python 3.12, standard library only):

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r420-all-length-cleanup-floor
```

The core command is `python3 -I -O -B research/r420-all-length-cleanup-floor/verify.py`, which prints `PASS_R420_ALL_LENGTH_CLEANUP_FLOOR lower=9 attained=9 adds=11 columns=6 boolean=64 controls=5`.

Validation passed on Python 3.14.7 and the full registered Python 3.12.15 replay. Two exact engines check the target, signed inverse, bound and witness. Eight mathematical/package tests include all 9,331 three-register words through length five, an actual 19-ADD same-target word, a free-SWAP scope counterexample, archive/receipt corruptions, refused receipt overwrite and relocated optimized replay. These finite checks validate implementation and the numerical instance; the universal statement follows from PROOF.md. The portable runtime was checked against its published digests. Staged whitespace and archive-to-Git provenance checks pass.

Exact base: `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`. Target source: PR1058 head `d148d200f2d64c90504fa3a9608e455aaa4c0c21`. Reused witness receipt: PR1266 commit `8edfb5d97aea03d26316964f35359d1864731dbe`, unchanged by its later attribution fix. Git blobs, source hashes, scope change and open next question are recorded in the package. [Discussion 1279](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1279) is the coordination claim.

The theorem fixes the exact integer lift, six ordered registers and positive ADD alphabet, excluding workspace and permutations. It optimizes the positive bound map for a common incoming coordinate budget. The matrices trade entries, so the result does not establish an improvement for the full circuit's nonuniform entering bounds. Whole-word native pricing, selected-supplier adoption and outer assembly remain integration obligations; no new kappa or full multiplication theorem is claimed.

Credit: **Chris Barber (@cbarber1)** for PR1058's target, circuit minimum and DAG; **Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337)** for PR1266's reused witness/envelope; **eumemic** for the underlying PR543 R420 architecture, with full inherited credit retained in the frozen NOTICE. New proof and package by Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Both verifier engines belong to this same AI-assisted contribution; no independent human review or proof-assistant formalization is implied. Apache-2.0.
